answer: Sybil resistance requires each claimed identity to complete a fresh chain of sequential modular squarings, where each result is needed before the next can be computed. GPUs may run separate clones concurrently, but cannot parallelize one clone’s dependency chain, so each added identity costs hardware and incurs an unavoidable wall-clock delay. A Wesolowski proof lets peers verify the work cheaply, whether identities are called tide, comet, or island.
